newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board for the second straight day on Tuesday due to new domestic A share issues and rising A share markets, traders said.

The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose sharply to 30 percent from 15.88 percent on Monday. The shortest three-day contract ended at a record high of 60 percent, up from Monday's 15.88 percent.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose slightly to 10.49 million lots from 10.48 million.
Three companies are issuing A shares on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges this week, pushing fund demand on the repo market dramatically up, traders said.
In addition, the A shares indices on the two bourses rose again on Tuesday, continuing a bull run since late February and strengthening market sentiment on the repo market, they said.
The bulk of the fund demand on the repo market has come from the A share markets.
Traders said a technical correction in the next few days was inevitable as the repo rates rose so sharply on Tuesday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Tuesday with the active A share markets sucking a lot of liquidity out of the spot market and pulling prices down.
The most active three-year bond maturing in August 1999 fell to 104.82 yuan from 104.90 yuan. Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 1.14 million lots from 1.07 million lots.
Traders said a strong bull run on the A share markets had begun to hurt the T-bill spot market.
"If there is no big institutional buying on the market, the prices won't go up in the short term," one trader said.
